samples.question: The image is a dense 32-by-32 lattice of bright and dark cells that looks like pure noise, but the noise is exactly symmetric about a 180-degree rotation (subtracting the rotated copy cancels the noise). A coarse diagonal-band glyph was written as an anti-symmetric brightness bias. Take the field and subtract its 180-degree-rotated copy; the surviving field is a clean diagonal band. Which glyph is revealed, A (rising /) or B (falling \)? Answer A or B.
